metadata.summary: Each year the International Day of Peace is observed around the world on 21 September. The General Assembly has declared this as a day devoted to strengthening the ideals of peace, both within and among all nations and peoples.
metadata.description: The Secretary-General and the President of the General Assembly will celebrate the International Day of Peace in the Peace Garden at United Nations Headquarters by ringing the Peace Bell and observing a minute of silence.

sentences.text: Excellencies, dear colleagues, friends, good morning.
I'm Melissa Fleming, UN Under-Secretary-General for Global Communications, and it is my honor to welcome you to this year's Peace Bell ceremony.
We gather in observation of International Peace Day.
It's commemorated every year on the 21st of September.
And this is a date on which, if only for one moment, we ask the world to pause and reflect on what peace truly means.
For our organization, this day carries special meaning.
It speaks to the deepest aspirations of humankind, and that is to live in a world free of violence and strife.
I would like to begin by thanking the young violinist from Tarumi Program and the United Nations Singers for the beautiful and inspiring music that they shared with us.
The theme of this year's observance is "Invest in Peace for Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day."

sentences.text: Thank you.
Thank you, Mr. Secretary General, and please join me now in welcoming the President of the General Assembly, His Excellency Mr. Khalilur Rahman.
And following his statement, the President of the General Assembly will also ring the Peace Bell.
Mr. Secretary General, Ambassador Yamazaki Madam Yamazaki, Under Secretary General Fleming, and all those gathered here at this monument of peace, peace be upon all of us.
I'm honored to join you today to commemorate the International Day of Peace.
Allow me to express my sincere thanks to Ambassador Yamazaki and the Permanent Mission of Japan for maintaining this venerable tradition.
We are privileged to be joined by Ms. Takase Siko, daughter of Peace Bell creator Chiyoji Nakagawa, who proposed his idea to the sixth session of the General Assembly in Paris in 1951.
Moved by an extraordinary aspiration for peace, Mr. Nakagawa collected coins from around the world, melted them, and cast the Peace Bell from the stories they told.
This is what he has done, stories of saving, lives and sacrifice, of solidarity in times of chaos, of hope that the seeds for global peace might one day take hold.
This hope for peace was placed in the hands of the United Nations, where we are standing today, and with it a duty to ensure it was not placed in vain.
